name: What layout challenges are common when updating appliances in older Denver-area homes?

mainEntity.name: What layout challenges are common when updating appliances in older Denver-area homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In older Denver and Aurora homes, original kitchen layouts often have inadequate electrical capacity, outdated wiring, and undersized range vents. Mid-century and historic houses frequently rely on 60- or 100-amp main panels that cannot support multiple high-draw appliances like induction ranges, double wall ovens, and built-in microwaves simultaneously. Remodeling often requires running home runs back to the panel or performing a service upgrade. Additionally, exterior wall framing in older properties may need custom furring or headers to accommodate modern ductwork and recessed utility boxes.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes often have limited electrical service, shallow framing, and lack dedicated venting, requiring panel upgrades and utility rework before installing modern appliances.
